question: Explain general relativity to a beginner through the question: why does gravity bend light?

scene.title:
Light takes the natural path.
Gravity changes the geometry.
scene.subtitle: An introduction to general relativity, one beam of light at a time.

beats.title: First, a universe without this mass.
beats.body: Follow the beam. With no nearby mass in this model, its path is straight. The faint line is our reference: where the light would go without the object.

beats.title: Now put something massive in its way.
beats.body: The mass changes the geometry of spacetime around it. Light follows a natural path through that geometry. From this distant view, the path bends toward the mass.

beats.title: Same light. A different route.
beats.body: Increase the mass, then move the beam farther away. More mass means more bending; a more distant pass means less. Light still travels at the speed of light when measured locally.

scene.takeaway: Gravity does not need to give light a rest mass. It changes the spacetime geometry that light travels through.

research.claim: A massive object changes the path of light passing nearby.
research.explanation: General relativity describes gravity through the geometry of spacetime. Light follows a null geodesic: the natural path for light in that geometry. Near a mass, that path can look bent when viewed from far away.
assumptions: Light passes far outside the strong-gravity region.
A first-order weak-field approximation; source and observer are treated as distant.
research.prediction: At the same passing distance, doubling the mass doubles the small deflection angle. At the same mass, doubling the passing distance halves it.
research.falsifier: A precise measurement of light deflection inconsistent with the predicted angle, after accounting for the mass, geometry and measurement uncertainty, would challenge this model in its stated regime.
limitations: Bending is magnified six times in the drawing.
This is not a black-hole simulation or a literal picture of curved spacetime.
The moving dot illustrates a path; its screen speed is not a physical measurement.
Passing these checks does not establish a new scientific result.

sources.title: Einstein Online · Gravitational deflection of light
sources.supports: General relativity predicts gravitational light deflection, tested with astronomical observations.

sources.title: Einstein Online · The equivalence principle and light
sources.supports: Local equivalence alone does not determine the full deflection; spacetime geometry matters.
